entries.observedDescription: The middle two ranks are quicksands. If one of your pieces ends the turn on the same square in the middle two ranks twice in a row, it can never move again
sampleDescriptions: The middle two ranks are quicksand. If one of your pieces ends the turn on the same square in the middle two ranks twice in a row, it can never move again
ambiguities: Twice in a row means consecutive affected-player end-turn snapshots. Runtime continuity uses piece type and square with moved-destination replacement protection; castling tracks the rook separately. Exact state cannot be reconstructed from only a final FEN and move list, so midgame initialization requires supplied state.

entries.observedDescription: If you moved a knight on your last move, you can't move a knight
sampleDescriptions: If you moved a knight on your last move, you can't move a knight

entries.observedDescription: You start being enable to capture. Every turn, you study all the pieces you would be able to capture normally, and once you studied them for a turn, you can capture that piece type for the rest of the game
sampleDescriptions: You start being unable to capture. Every turn, you study all the pieces you would be able to capture normally, and once you've studied them for a turn, you can capture that piece type for the rest of the game
ambiguities: A target type becomes unlocked after completing a turn on which at least one standard-legal capture of that type was available, so it cannot be captured on the first study turn.
Study uses standard-legal rather than pseudo-legal captures and persists for the rest of the game.
Capturing promotions are classified by the captured target type; en-passant studies and captures pawns.
Exact initialization from an arbitrary midgame move list is impossible because unplayed historical capture opportunities are absent; chronological play from the game start is exact.

entries.observedDescription: You can only move non-pawns to squares whose opposition square reflected across the center line is occupied
ambiguities: Center line means the horizontal line between ranks four and five, mapping a1 to a8; a vertical or rotational interpretation is possible.
Occupancy is evaluated in the pre-move position and either color counts.
Promotion is classified by its pawn mover and castling by the primary king destination.

entries.observedDescription: If you can move a piece that's adjacent to the destination of your last move, you must
ambiguities: Adjacency is measured before the move and includes diagonals. Castling history uses the king destination.

sampleDescriptions: If your opponent moves a bishop, you must move a bishop (or lose)

sampleDescriptions: Every 10 turns, the water level rises one rank. You can't move pieces that are underwater and you can't move to squares that are underwater
ambiguities: Turns are counted separately for the affected player. Water rises from White's rank 1 and Black's rank 8 after each block of ten completed affected-player moves.

entries.observedDescription: You can't move your rooks until you connected them

entries.observedDescription: You must promote to rooks. Your king and queen cannot move diagonally
sampleDescriptions: You must promote to rooks. Your king and queen cannot move diagonally

entries.observedDescription: You can only move a total of 100 distance. Once you run out, you lose
sampleDescriptions: You can only move a total of 100 distance. Once you run out, you lose

Standard checkmate on the final-unit move ends the game before that later loss can occur. If every legal move costs more than the remaining budget, the generic no-drawback-legal-move loss applies.
